# Time Continuity

## 1 · The First Instant

Write the instant the Cut begins, not the action it ends on.

- The still is that Cut's first frame, so a still for 'turns their head and looks at the sea' that already shows the head turned leaves the clip nothing to do for its whole 3–8 seconds.
- **When you want a climax standing as a picture, split the Cut and make the climax the first instant of the next one.** Do not write it into the description of the Cut it happens in — that is how film emphasises in the first place.

*The test:* every description could be a photograph taken the moment the Cut starts.

## 2 · The World Survives

The Scene's world has to survive from one Cut to the next.

- A large prop that drives the event carries its state at that instant in every Cut from the one it enters to the one it leaves — airborne just before landing, settled with the rotors still turning, rotors stopped. Miss it in one Cut and it disappears from that Cut entirely. Writing only its effect is also missing it: 'the wind the helicopter threw up' becomes a person shielding their forehead on an empty deck.
- **A beat where two people touch needs the distance and the touch between them written down.** Leave it out and 'does not take the offered hand' is drawn as two people several steps apart, each facing the camera.
- **Nail whatever this work has to hold into the first sentence** — the helmet under an arm, which side the scar is on, the letters on a name tag. Inside one Draft, the Scenes that pinned action and props Cut by Cut ran visibly better, and only the Scenes whose text did not pin the world fell apart.

*The test:* a reader could list every object in the Scene and say where each one is in every Cut.

## 3 · What Travels

Four things travel between Cuts, and only one of them is stored.

- The still pass reads every Cut in the Scene at once, so each Cut receives the world at its own first instant. The clip pass carries the camera movement and the motion the Cut description names, and adds the next Cut's first instant in the same Scene as the arrival point — a Scene's last Cut settles and closes. These three are built just before generation, so fixing the text is enough: the next generation receives the new sentence.
- **animaticPrompt is the fourth, and it does stay in the field.** The board bake writes it for a Scene with two or more Cuts, out of the same reading as the three above, so it cannot contradict the sentence the still receives. Reading it back and correcting it is step 3 of animatics.md.
- **A Cut's first instant is attached only when the Scene has two or more Cuts.** Redraw a single Cut with regenerate_cut and there is no neighbour to join to, so that Cut is drawn without it. When the redraw is meant to fix a boundary, give regenerate_board that Scene's id instead.

*The test:* you fixed the text, not the generation, and know which of the four carried it.

## 4 · The Camera Cannot

The camera cannot rise, fall, or move closer — build it from the subject and its surroundings.

- Crane Up or Crane Down produces a Dolly, in which background and subject grow in proportion: five runs out of five on the same Cut and the same first frame, and a rule-abiding prompt did not save it either. Tilt is no substitute — only one of two runs carried a vertical axis at all, and neither carried the intended direction. For a sinking Cut, write the pair into animaticPrompt instead: 'the body toward the lower edge, the droplets toward the upper'. It saves with one warning, because what lost is the video model currently attached rather than the value.
- **A camera moving closer cannot come out either — carry the weight with something small on screen, or with Cut length.** Dolly In produces a still frame, and shortening the movement sentence, halving the pacing and dropping the last line all did it, four runs out of four, so no prompt saves this. **Dolly Out came out in all four runs.** Where the Cut description already holds a body in motion, leave the movement Static: that action fills the screen, and the camera sentence was only competing with it.
- **Do not invent a body a still face or object never had.** A name-tag insert, a console screen, a listening face — a name tag cannot come toward the camera, and a listener who suddenly leans in loses whatever that Cut was for. What such a Cut wanted from Dolly In was not the approach but the weight of 'look at this'. Carry it by writing something small into animaticPrompt (an eye blinks once, a line of screen text scrolls, light travels across a metal surface), or by accepting a still Cut and giving **Cut length** the upper end of that beat's range.
- **These three stay among the advertised options — they are a place to measure again when the model changes.** A different video model was the exact opposite: Dolly In in all four runs, Dolly Out in only one of four.
- **Leaving the clip field blank does not get you out of it.** A blank clip movement makes the video use the Storyboard field's cameraMovement, so a Crane written there still goes out. The video doors (animate_cut, animate_draft) measure **the movement this clip will actually go out with** and raise one warning per Cut then, one even when both fields say Crane. The still doors (generate_storyboard, finalize_render) stay quiet — the measurements came from video only, and nobody has yet measured what Crane draws on a still.

*The test:* no Cut asks the camera to do something this model answers with a still frame.

## 5 · You Check the Boundaries

Nobody checks the boundaries but you.

- **The joining meshes only when the place the clip heads toward and the place the next Cut's still drew are the same.** In a Draft whose stills were baked before these features, the clip goes to a place the still never drew — there the hand prescription above still holds, and the root fix is re-baking that Scene's stills.
- **A boundary that jumps several shot sizes (Full → Close-Up) is not caught automatically.** The next Cut's first instant is a sentence true only in the next Cut's frame, so a frame three steps away receives it and the two disagree. Look at those boundaries yourself.
- **When a boundary is in doubt, put the previous clip's last moment beside the next clip's first and ask whether it is the same world** — the prop that was there before, how many people and where, the same costume. review_clips names first frame and last frame separately; its paid scale and skipping are in animatics.md.
- **Fix a diverged boundary in the text before re-baking.** Nail the world at that instant into the first sentence of the later Cut's description, and write where that prop is into the earlier Cut's. Re-baking with nothing changed upstream is a lottery, and a paid one.
- **Rule Check does not look at this axis — deliberately.** Whether a prop disappeared can only be judged by knowing what it means, which cannot be made precise as a single rule, and a half-made warning kills the whole rulebook. Do not read the absence of a warning as the boundaries being sound: what has been looked at is only what you looked at. A paid full audit that counts the whole Draft runs on the director's side (`backend/scripts/continuity/boundary_audit.py`), and the Assistant Director has no such hand, so say so when asked for a full count.

*The test:* every boundary you called sound is one you actually put side by side.

Complete when: Every Cut description in the touched Scene opens at that shot's first instant instead of its finished action, every event prop carries its own state in each Cut from the one it enters to the one it leaves, and every contact beat states the distance and touch between the people. No Cut asks the camera to rise, fall, or move closer: every rise or fall is built from the subject and its surroundings, and every push toward a subject is carried either by motion the Cut description already holds or by the Cut's own length, because this video model turns Crane into a dolly, Tilt into neither axis nor direction, and Dolly In into a still frame. No still insert, screen, or listening face was given a body it did not have in order to replace that push. Every boundary the director doubted was checked by putting one clip's last moment beside the next clip's first and was corrected in the Cut text before any paid regeneration, and a Draft whose stills predate this continuity work — or a boundary that jumps several shot sizes — was named as needing eyes rather than reported as covered.
